name: Should an ADU kitchen include a pantry or use cabinet storage only?

mainEntity.name: Is a separate pantry worth giving up space in a small ADU kitchen?
mainEntity.text: Is a separate pantry worth giving up space in a small ADU kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether an ADU kitchen should include a pantry depends on the unit size and how the space will be used. In larger ADUs, a small pantry can be a strong feature because it keeps dry goods, small appliances, and bulk items organized. In compact ADUs, however, a dedicated pantry room or deep walk-in cabinet may waste square footage that would be better used for counter space, circulation, or a larger living area. Tall pantry cabinets, pull-out shelves, and appliance garages often give much of the same benefit in a more efficient footprint. The best solution is usually the one that fits the unit’s daily use patterns. If the ADU is meant for long-term occupancy, extra storage may be worth the space. If the unit is highly compact or rental-focused, integrated storage is often the smarter choice. A good design should make the kitchen easy to live with every day, not just impressive on the plan.
acceptedAnswer.description: A separate pantry is helpful if the ADU has enough floor area to support it, but many small kitchens work better with integrated cabinet storage. In compact ADUs, tall pantry cabinets or pull-out storage often provide the same function without consuming valuable circulation space.
